boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Rochester rituals, ceremonies, and recurring campus events.

cards.title: Meliora Weekend
cards.subtitle: Fall reunion, family, and homecoming weekend
cards.notes: Look for the fall program that brings alumni, families, students, faculty, staff, and friends back together for campus events.
cards.short_summary: A fall weekend combining reunion, family, and homecoming programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says Meliora Weekend was founded in 2001 and combines reunion, family weekend, and homecoming activities.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Programming and access vary by event.

cards.title: Commencement Weekend
cards.subtitle: University-wide graduation ceremony at Fauver Stadium
cards.notes: If visiting at graduation time, see the University-wide ceremony that gathers graduates at Fauver Stadium for formal celebration.
cards.short_summary: The University-wide graduation observance centered on Fauver Stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Commencement Weekend as a University-wide ceremony at Fauver Stadium marking students' transition to graduates.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Held during Commencement Weekend; ceremony access may be managed for attendees.

cards.title: Boar’s Head Dinner
cards.subtitle: Annual medieval-inspired December dinner
cards.notes: Follow the December tradition where a River Campus venue becomes a medieval-style court with student performances and a formal feast.
cards.short_summary: A student tradition dating to 1934, built around a medieval-inspired dinner.
cards.evidence_claim: University reporting says the Boar’s Head Dinner began in 1934, runs annually with few exceptions, and is open to undergraduates.
cards.source_title: Boar’s Head Dinner: A URochester tradition that goes way back in time
cards.access_notes: Held annually in December; tickets have limited availability.

cards.title: Painting the Tunnels
cards.subtitle: Eastman Quad tunnel tradition
cards.notes: Walk through the Eastman Quad tunnel to view student-organization announcements, then check the painted walls as messages change over time.
cards.short_summary: Student organizations use the tunnel walls to announce events and raise awareness.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says Eastman Quad tunnel painting began in the 1970s and is used by student organizations for announcements and awareness.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Use normal campus pedestrian access and posted tunnel guidelines.

cards.title: Wilson Day and Eastman Day
cards.subtitle: Fall community-service tradition for new students
cards.notes: Watch for Welcome Week service projects that connect incoming students with Rochester community organizations and local partners.
cards.short_summary: A fall service tradition honoring Joseph C. Wilson and George Eastman.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies Wilson Day and Eastman Day as fall community-service events for first-year and incoming students honoring the two benefactors.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Participation details are organized through Welcome Week and community-engagement programming.

cards.title: Winterfest Weekend
cards.subtitle: Winter campus programming
cards.notes: Check the winter schedule for outdoor-focused programming, including marshmallow roasting, ice carving, and student performances.
cards.short_summary: A campus winter celebration with seasonal activities and performances.
cards.evidence_claim: The University lists Winterfest Weekend as a tradition featuring marshmallow roasting, live ice carving, and student performances.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Event offerings and locations vary by year.

cards.title: Candlelight Ceremony
cards.subtitle: First-night gathering around Eastman Quad
cards.notes: Incoming students gather around Eastman Quad by candlelight to hear about Rochester’s history and traditions on their first night.
cards.short_summary: A first-night orientation ceremony centered on Eastman Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the incoming class surrounds Eastman Quad during this first-night tradition to learn institutional history and traditions by candlelight.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Designed for the incoming class during orientation programming.

cards.title: Clock Tower Superstition
cards.subtitle: Dandelion Square and the George Eastman statue
cards.notes: See the Clock Tower and George Eastman statue, then read the campus legend linking a walk beneath the tower to an acorn remedy.
cards.short_summary: A campus legend involving Dandelion Square’s clock tower and George Eastman statue.
cards.evidence_claim: The University documents the legend that walking under the Dandelion Square clock tower brings misfortune, with an acorn toss as the stated remedy.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Observe the site respectfully; the superstition is presented by the University as a legend.

cards.title: Convocation + Class Roll Signing
cards.subtitle: Joining the University community in writing
cards.notes: After Convocation, incoming students sign their class roll; look for preserved rolls in Rush Rhees Library at later milestones.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic enrollment ritual whose class rolls are preserved in the library.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says students sign the class roll after Convocation, and that the rolls are preserved in Rush Rhees Library and displayed at Commencement and reunions.
cards.source_title: Symbols and Traditions | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: Class-roll signing follows Convocation; later displays occur at specified University milestones.

cards.title: Dandelion Day
cards.subtitle: Springfest Community Weekend campus carnival
cards.notes: Visit during Springfest Community Weekend for the campus tradition built around rides, games, food, music, and a scheduled performance.
cards.short_summary: A spring campus carnival held as part of Springfest Community Weekend.
cards.evidence_claim: The University identifies Dandelion Day as a campus tradition within Springfest Community Weekend, with food, rides, music, and activities.
cards.source_title: Dandelion Day FAQ | University of Rochester
cards.access_notes: The University’s FAQ says activities run during the day and start at 2 p.m.; check the current event schedule.
